'''Thomas Carlos Mehen''' (September 8, 1970 - December 29, 2024) was an American physicist.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomas Carlos Mehen Obituary (2025) - Hillsborough, NC - Endswell Aquamation Cremation |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/thomas-mehen-obituary?id=57219971 |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> His research consisted of primarily [[quantum chromodynamics]] (QCD) and the application of effective field theory to problems in [[hadronic]] physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomas C. Mehen {{!}} Scholars@Duke profile |url=https://scholars.duke.edu/person/mehen |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=scholars.duke.edu |language=en}}</ref> He also worked on effective field theory for non-relativistic particles whose short range interactions are characterized by a large scattering length, as well as novel field theories which arise from unusual limits of [[string theory]]. He died of natural causes on December 29, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Communications |first=Trinity |date=December 31, 2024 |title=Physics Professor Tom Mehen Passes Away {{!}} Trinity College of Arts & Sciences |url=https://trinity.duke.edu/news/physics-professor-tom-mehen-passes-away |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=trinity.duke.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Mehen was born in Tegucigalpa, Honduras where he learned Spanish as his [[first language]]. His parents were Thomas and Elizabeth Mehen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elizabeth Mehen Obituary - Falls Church, VA |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/falls-church-va/elizabeth-mehen-9206265 |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=Dignity Memorial |language=en-us}}</ref> In 1974 at the age of three he relocated with his family to [[McLean, Virginia]], USA. 

== Career ==
Mehen was educated at the [[University of Virginia]] (B.S., 1992), and [[Johns Hopkins University]] (M.A., Ph.D., 1998).<ref>{{cite thesis|title=Phenomenology of heavy quarks and quarkonium|first=Thomas Carlos|last=Mehen|date=1 July 1998|degree=Ph.D.|pages=1–277|bibcode=1998PhDT.......249M}}</ref> He served as a research associate and [[John A. McCone]] Postdoctoral Scholar in the Division of Mathematics, Physics and Astronomy at the [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1997 to 2000. He served as a research associate and University Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Physics at the [[Ohio State University]] from 2000–2001. In 2002 he joined the Department of Physics at [[Duke University]] as assistant professor,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehen |first=Thomas |date=2024 |title=CV of Thomas Mehen |url=https://webhome.phy.duke.edu/~mehen/CV.pdf}}</ref> being promoted up to full professor in 2016. He also served as a visiting professor at [[Duke Kunshan University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Duke Physics: Tom Mehen's Webpage |url=https://webhome.phy.duke.edu/~mehen/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506231702/https://webhome.phy.duke.edu/~mehen/ |archive-date=2021-05-06 |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=webhome.phy.duke.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://fds.duke.edu/db/aas/Physics/mehen|title=Duke Physics}}</ref> 

In 2005 Mehen received an Outstanding Junior Investigator Award in Nuclear Physics by the [[United States Department of Energy]].<ref>[http://www.science.doe.gov/np/program/oji.html Outstanding Junior Investigator Program] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304013910/http://www.science.doe.gov/np/program/oji.html |date=March 4, 2009 }}, The Office of Nuclear Physics, United States Department of Energy</ref> He contributed almost [https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=25&page=1&q=a%20t%20mehen&ui-citation-summary=true 100 published works] and was a lecturer in his field.<ref>http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?rawcmd=ea+Mehen,+Thomas {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/997921 |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>
